newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CS Reseach cuts Nestle forecast again.
newsitem.headline: CS Reseach cuts Nestle forecast again.

text.p: CS Equity Research said it was cutting its earnings forecast for Nestle for the second time in a week in light of the company's "disappointing operating performance" in the first half of 1996.
But it maintained its "neutral" rating for shares even though it expected them to stay under short-term sales pressure.
CS last week cut its 1996 estimated earnings per share (EPS) by 2.2 Swiss francs to 84.3 and its 1997 EPS by 0.8 franc to 91.1.
"We are now making a further reduction of a similar proportion and magnitude: 1996E EPS is now 82.8 Swiss francs, 1997E EPS is 90.5 francs," it said in a research note.
At 1400 GMT, the food and beverages group's registered shares were changing hands at 1,399 Swiss francs, down 14 from the close.

CS said its earnings model put the 12-month target for the shares at barely more than 1,400 francs, but added the nearly 20 percent discount to Anglo-Dutch consumer products group Unilever Plc would support Nestle shares.
"Moreover, the current p/e of Nestle at 15.6 (1997E) represents only a four percent premium over the Swiss Market Index (15.0) which is Nestle's historic position," it added.
"As such we continue to feel a 12-month target of 1,450 Swiss francs and a current fair value price of 1,375-1,400 for the registered shares to be reasonable," it said.
The report said a further short-term correction was likely, not just for fundamental valuation reasons but also because psychology was working against Nestle.

"The absence of either good news or investment fantasy will likely lead to apathy selling. Additionally, many other analysts are known to be reducing their estimates. Others have also now abandoned their "buy" recommendations. We remain "neutral" on the stock," it said.
